name: Genode OS Framework
summary: Modular open-source operating system framework founded on a microkernel architecture and capability-based security, organising its services into a hierarchical tree of strictly isolated components.
license: Open Source (GNU Affero General Public License v3 with commercial licence options)

content.introduction: Genode (Genode OS Framework) is a free modular operating system framework written in C++. Initiated in 2008 by Norman Feske and Christian Helmuth within the German company Genode Labs, the project stems from academic research carried out at the Dresden University of Technology (TU Dresden). Genode aims to go beyond the structural vulnerabilities of traditional monolithic systems by designing the operating system not as an all-powerful block of code, but as a structured architectural environment making it possible to assemble independent software components under strict capability control.
content.what_is_it: Technically, Genode is neither a Linux distribution nor a conventional Unix-type system. It is a system infrastructure framework that organises all operating functionality (device drivers, file systems, display managers, network stacks and application environments) in the form of a recursive hierarchical tree of isolated components (component tree). The initial root component allocates to its children strict resource quotas and exclusive access rights (capabilities), guaranteeing that each component can interact only with the services for which an explicit authorisation has been delegated to it.
content.release_archive_and_source_hosting_histo: The release notes archive published by the project covers versions 8.11 to 26.08: the numbering associates the year and the month there, and the entries recorded for 2026 are 26.02, 26.05 and 26.08, the latter covering notably VirtualBox 7.2.14 and a Linux driver environment 6.18.19. The move of code hosting is also documented there: release note 26.02 indicates that the first half of the migration from GitHub to Codeberg is complete, and the page of the GitHub repository genodelabs/genode carries the mention of an archiving on 20 May 2026 with transfer to read-only; the corresponding Codeberg repository is active and its README mentions the complementary repository genode-world.
content.capability_security_model_and_component_: The Genode security model rests on the principle of least privilege applied through typed capabilities verified in hardware by the microkernel. No universal superuser (root) process exists in the system. Each parent component plays the role of regulating authority for its child processes: it controls their physical memory consumption, their processor time and their communication channels through remote procedure calls (RPC). This rigorous partitioning prevents by design any privilege escalation or lateral movement by an attacker: the compromise of a hardware driver or a network service remains strictly confined to its subtree without being able to contaminate the rest of the system.
content.kernel_agnostic_architecture_and_support: One of the remarkable particularities of Genode lies in its independence from the underlying kernel (kernel-agnostic). Thanks to a uniform abstraction layer, Genode can be deployed indifferently on several microkernels according to robustness or certification constraints: NOVA (micro-hypervisor highly optimised for x86 virtualisation), seL4 (microkernel formally verified mathematically for critical systems), Fiasco.OC (microkernel of the L4 family), Linux (used as a test bed in user space for rapid prototyping) or base-hw (the minimalist microkernel developed internally by Genode Labs to run directly on the silicon without external dependency).
content.sculpt_os_desktop_and_sandboxed_drivers: For desktop and laptop computers, Genode offers **Sculpt OS** (*Sculpt for The Curious*). Sculpt offers an original interactive graphical interface allowing the component tree to be visualised as a dynamic graph and storage devices, Wi-Fi cards, graphical interfaces and virtual machines to be interconnected at runtime. To ensure compatibility with contemporary computer hardware, Genode encapsulates complete hardware drivers from the Linux kernel or from OpenBSD (notably for Wi-Fi, Ethernet and USB controllers) within restricted environments (DDE - Device Driver Environment), neutralising any risk of kernel panic in case of hardware failure.
content.software_ecosystem_and_hardware_portabil: Although independent of Unix, Genode provides a standard C library (`libc`) and a POSIX interface emulation layer allowing the porting of ordinary applications (Falkon web browser, command-line utilities, web servers). It also makes it possible to launch isolated Linux or Windows virtual machines within unprivileged components through its virtual machine monitor (VMM). The framework is distributed under the free **GNU AGPLv3** licence (with commercial licences available from Genode Labs) and runs on the x86-32, x86-64, ARM (ARMv7 and AArch64) and RISC-V hardware architectures.
content.diffusion_de_sculpt_et_cycle_de_publicat: Genode is distributed mainly through Sculpt OS, whose current version at the time of consultation is 26.04, published in April 2026 in the form of a 35 MiB disk image accompanied by its signature and its public key. The image is written to a USB key with dd under Unix systems, or with Rufus or Win32 Disk Imager under Windows. Two complementary variants are published: an experimental version of Sculpt for the PinePhone, distributed by the Genode Labs repository, and an image for the MNT Reform laptop in i.MX8 variant. The components do not come from an external package manager: they are supplied by federated providers and installed from the component graph of the Leitzentrale administration interface, which also carries the system update and the rollback to a previous version.
content.installation_and_tool_chain: Building the framework goes through a dedicated tool chain: the project states that the GNU compilers supplied by the distributions are not suitable, because of distribution-specific patches and of the local thread storage configuration, and therefore provides its own chain. Precompiled binaries exist for Debian 12.10 and for Ubuntu 24.04, each with its SHA-256 fingerprint; the archive is extracted with `sudo tar xPf genode-toolchain-<version>-<os>.tar.xz` and installed in `/usr/local/genode/tool/<version>`, the location expected by the build system. The chain has been unified since version 11.11 for x86_32, x86_64, ARM, aarch64 and RISC-V, and the tools carry the prefixes `genode-x86-`, `genode-arm-`, `genode-riscv-` and `genode-aarch64-`. A build from source remains possible with `tool/tool_chain`.
content.depot_and_package_provisioning: Software supply relies on a public repository distinct from the system images: the index of the depot.genode.org server lists directories by provider, among which genodelabs and skalk, both modified on 13 October 2026, cproc_test, modified on 19 October 2026, as well as alex-ab, atopia, chelmuth, cnuke, jschlatow, mstein, nfeske and ssumpf. Release note 26.08 explicitly places an experimental package, `goa_offline_sdk`, in the repository of provider cproc for Sculpt 26.04, which ties the content of a repository to a system version. The main source tree is complemented by the genode-world repository, described by the project as a growing library of additional software that can be integrated into component scenarios.
advantages: Highly secure component architecture founded on capabilities and the principle of least privilege.
Kernel agnosticism making it possible to run indifferently on seL4, NOVA, base-hw or Linux.
Complete isolation of hardware drivers in user space (no risk of system crash in case of a driver bug).
Dynamic desktop system Sculpt OS offering visual and interactive management of the component tree.
Ability to host Linux and Windows virtual machines in partitioned micro-components.
Major multi-architecture portability covering x86-64, ARM64 and RISC-V under the free GNU AGPLv3 licence.
disadvantages: Demanding learning curve breaking radically with the conventions of conventional Unix/Linux operating systems.
Restricted native application catalogue requiring POSIX emulation layers or virtual machines for complex software.
Support for complex hardware 3D graphics acceleration still being perfected.
Textual or Sculpt-graph system configuration requiring a solid background in operating system engineering.
Not intended for the general public looking for an immediately familiar mainstream distribution.
who_is_it_for: Researchers, system architects and cybersecurity engineers exploring capability architectures and formal resilience.
Developers of critical systems and industrial computing (automotive, telecoms, defence, aerospace).
Enthusiasts of alternative architectures wishing to use a genuinely partitioned workstation through Sculpt OS.
Advanced users looking for a computing environment in which no process holds absolute privileges.
who_is_it_not_for: Beginner users looking for a conventional desktop system of the Windows, macOS or Ubuntu type.
Players of recent PC video games depending on proprietary graphics drivers and closed anti-cheats.
Administrators of cloud computing infrastructures requiring standard Linux container orchestrators.
Professionals depending on proprietary office or creative suites that cannot be virtualised.
content.verdict: Genode OS Framework is an operating system framework founded on the principle of capability-based security. It organises independent components in a hierarchical tree above a microkernel, as an alternative to traditional monolithic kernels, and serves as the basis for general-purpose or specialised systems.
